Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-022.md for WF02-REQ-022 (withdraw from a registration and free the seat) at branch feature/WF02-REQ-022, commit 330d724. Scope test: Step 2's artifacts_out (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's new decideWithdrawOutcome/withdrawRegistration/getRegistrationForEventAndUser exports plus the modified registerForEvent row-reuse path; apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts, new file, the /withdraw command + withdraw:confirm/withdraw:cancel callbacks; apps/bot/src/index.ts's three new handler registrations; apps/bot/src/i18n/{types,ru,en}.ts's new Catalog.withdraw section) is real user-visible/behavioral surface -- a real confirmation prompt, two real buttons, and real registrations/audit_log writes (or the deliberate absence of one). Full Steps 3b/4 apply.

Read docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md, WF-02_requirement_implementation.md Step 3, docs/guides/qa_testing_guide.md, docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-021.md (reference shape) and REQ-020.md (harness boilerplate source), docs/agents/design/REQ-022.md in full, apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts (decideWithdrawOutcome, withdrawRegistration, getRegistrationForEventAndUser, and the modified registerForEvent, lines 306-436 and the row-reuse diff at lines 138-219), apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts (all three handlers in full), the real apps/bot/src/i18n/en.ts/ru.ts/types.ts withdraw catalog block (quoted verbatim), apps/bot/src/index.ts's registration lines, and BACKEND-DEV's already-committed apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts lines 540-808 (its own REQ-022 decideWithdrawOutcome unit block plus the AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5 DB-backed describe blocks) so this spec's cases are independently parameterized, not accidental duplicates.

Each of the 5 acceptance criteria has at least one concrete, judgment-free verification case, plus a 6th case (AC-security) added per this run's explicit instruction closing the coverage gap SECURITY-REVIEWER flagged. Per this project's convention (REQ-019/REQ-020/REQ-021's precedent), none of them merely points at BACKEND-DEV's already-committed tests -- every case is this spec's own, with its own exact fixture values (own uuids, own tg_id range 1000000500+, different capacities than BACKEND-DEV's fixtures) and closes gaps nothing committed exercises: no existing test dispatches a real Telegram command/callback through handlers/withdraw.ts at all (BACKEND-DEV's suite calls decideWithdrawOutcome/withdrawRegistration/registerForEvent as plain functions throughout), so every case below is a live-dispatch case through the real handler chain.

Case-by-case:
- AC1 (confirmation required; dismissing leaves admission unchanged): live /withdraw dispatch showing the real prompt with its real two-button keyboard, then both the withdraw:cancel path (checking admission/audit-count fully unchanged) and the withdraw:confirm path (checking admission flips to withdrawn with exactly one new audit row), both through the real callback handlers with exact reply-text checks.
- AC-security (the flagged gap): constructs an Owner (registers for real) and an Attacker (no registration of their own), dispatches withdraw:confirm:<owner's real registrationId> AS THE ATTACKER via real bot.handleUpdate(), and asserts (a) the owner's row is completely unchanged (admission AND updated_at, read back explicitly), (b) zero new audit rows of any kind, and (c) the reply text is byte-identical to a second, same-script comparison dispatch naming a genuinely nonexistent registration id -- proving no disclosure that the forged id was real/owned by someone else. This closes exactly the gap SECURITY-REVIEWER named: decideWithdrawOutcome's not-owner branch had only ever been unit-tested against its return value, never proven through the actual callback handler with real Postgres state.
- AC2 (seats-left +1 at next read): capacity=2 (BACKEND-DEV used capacity=1), fills the event via real register callbacks, withdraws one via the real confirm callback, reads the admitted-row count via two independent SQL queries before/after (delta of exactly one, not inferred from a single diff), then has a third user register via the real callback to prove the freed seat is genuinely usable (admitted, not waitlisted).
- AC3 (checked-in refusal, row unchanged): registers via real callback, sets checked_in_at via direct SQL (per this run's own instruction, since check-in is a separate command not being re-tested here), dispatches the real withdraw:confirm callback, and checks the exact refusedCheckedIn text plus admission/checked_in_at both unchanged and zero new audit rows.
- AC4 (re-register UPDATEs the same row): full register -> withdraw-confirm -> re-register cycle dispatched entirely through real callbacks (never registerForEvent/withdrawRegistration called directly, unlike BACKEND-DEV's two DB-level cases), checking exact id/created_at equality and a single-row count for the (event,user) pair.
- AC5 (exactly one audit_log row per withdrawal): not a new dispatch -- an explicit before/after audit-count table built from AC1/AC-security/AC3's own read-backs (dismiss=0, confirm=+1, forged-cross-user=0, checked-in=0), so TEST-RUNNER must quote all four deltas explicitly rather than inferring AC5 from the other cases' pass/fail alone.
- AC-schema and AC-catalog (mechanical, added beyond the 5 ACs per this project's REQ-020/021 precedent): git diff --stat on apps/bot/drizzle (expect empty, per design's explicit no-schema-change claim); grep-based parity check of the 9 new withdraw.* keys across all three i18n files (27/27 expected matches) and the 3 new handler registrations in index.ts.

Noted ISS-0014's --no-file-parallelism requirement explicitly in the spec's own execution-note section for TEST-RUNNER, and pointed TEST-RUNNER at REQ-020.md's Shared Setup step 6 for the harness boilerplate rather than re-pasting a third copy of the same script, to avoid the three specs' harnesses drifting apart.

Gap found while reading: none beyond the one this run's instructions already named and this spec closes (AC-security). No design or implementation defect found -- nothing new to file under ISSUE_QUEUE.md from this step.
